summary: Minimal stateless Node.js 22 HTTP health service using only built-in http and node:test. Exported server factory (src/app.cjs) is separate from executable startup (src/index.cjs). npm test runs real HTTP requests on an ephemeral loopback port; npm run build syntax-checks source via node --check. CommonJS .cjs conventions throughout.

tasks.description: Exported HTTP server factory in src/app.cjs: creates an http.Server whose request handler returns 200 JSON {"status":"ok"} for GET /health and 404 JSON error for any other route, with Content-Type application/json.

contracts.description: Module exports a createServer() factory returning an http.Server configured with the route handler; no listening side effects.
health route responds HTTP 200 with JSON body {"status":"ok"}; unknown routes respond HTTP 404 with a JSON error body.

tasks.description: Executable startup entry src/index.cjs: imports the factory, reads process.env.PORT defaulting to 3000, and listens so the process stays alive.

contracts.description: Startup entry listens on process.env.PORT (default 3000); kept separate from the factory so tests do not open a fixed port.

tasks.description: package.json declaring type commonjs, scripts (start, test, build), and engine Node.js >=22. build runs node --check on each .cjs source file.

contracts.description: npm start executes the startup entry on PORT; npm run build runs node --check on all source .cjs files; npm test runs the test file.

tasks.description: Real ephemeral-port HTTP tests in test/health.test.cjs using node:test and built-in http client: assert GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"}, unknown route returns 404 JSON, and a follow-up /health still returns 200; close the server after tests.

contracts.description: Tests listen on loopback port 0 (ephemeral) and exercise real HTTP behavior, never mocks; server is closed after test completion.

tasks.description: README.md with install/start/test instructions and a source-to-requirement mapping table.

contracts.description: README includes install, start, test instructions and a small source-to-requirement mapping.

assumptions: No database, Docker, identity provider, third-party packages, or cloud infrastructure are used; the design explicitly excludes them.
The JSON error body shape (e.g. {"error":"not found"}) is not specified by the source, so a minimal {"error":"not found"} is chosen (origin=assumption).
The build script uses node --check rather than a bundler/transpiler, since the service is plain CommonJS with no third-party tooling.
Content-Type is set to application/json for all responses to keep JSON semantics unambiguous.
